overall_summary: Analysis across 47 deduplicated shorts shows clear audience polarization: immersive first-person hypotheticals ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme cosmic anomaly survival hooks consistently capture 800-1,000+ views and 25-38 likes, whereas repeated uploads, passive biology trivia (e.g., octopus hearts, shark age), and generic psychology facts generate fewer than 100 views with virtually zero engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) outperformed channel baselines by over 500%.
winning_patterns.action: Frame cosmic and extreme scientific phenomena through immediate sensory survival stakes ('What would happen to your body if...').

winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,031 views, 36 likes, 2 comments) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (725 views, 25 likes) had top-tier like ratios (~3.5%) within 19-21s runtimes.
winning_patterns.action: Target 19-21 second runtimes detailing singular, visceral physical extremes paired with vivid comparative imagery.

weak_patterns.pattern: Repeated Uploads and Stale Brain/Psychology Trivia
weak_patterns.evidence: Duplicate uploads of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' tanked at 5 to 53 views; 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' repeatedly collapsed to 34-87 views.
weak_patterns.action: Cease duplicate re-uploads and phase out low-stakes psychology factoids that lack cinematic urgency or visual payoff.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (118 views, 0 likes) and 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' (69 views, 0 likes) flatlined across multiple iterations.
weak_patterns.action: Replace static animal trivia with high-stakes cinematic animal survival micro-stories or predatory evolutionary adaptations.
